verdict.rationale: cfo.ai documents a live model that pulls actuals from connected ledgers, refreshes nightly, and is 'rebuilt overnight off the close.' It also lets users re-import past months after fixing their books, so the model stays current without manual rebuilding. However, the docs never describe how forecast periods re-baseline: closed months swapping from forecast to actual, or drivers rolling forward. All evidence is vendor-claimed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of forecast re-baselining mechanics after a close (actuals replacing forecast periods, rolling horizon), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, the forecast re-baselines on fresh actuals after each close without rebuilding the model

citations.quote: One live model of the company, rebuilt overnight off the close, instead of a spreadsheet that is accurate on the day someone last had time to update it.
Bring in Actuals from QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, or Rillet.
re-import past months after you fix them in your books, and change the time a connection refreshes each night.
Ari builds the model and keeps it current, then messages you when something moves rather than waiting to be asked.
